name: Brutalist hero (mobile-fit): paper + terracotta, no-scroll on any device
notes: Second brutalist hero — paired with 0012 as the same design language in a different register: light paper ground instead of black, terracotta signal instead of safety-yellow, condensed Bebas Neue instead of blocky Archivo Black, a different real photo (a graphic architectural roofline, not a concrete building). Built specifically so every element — header, image, headline, dek, CTAs, stat row — is visible on one mobile screen with zero scrolling: the whole layout is a single-column flex column pinned to height:100svh, and every font-size/padding/gap uses a clamp() with an svh component so it scales down on short viewports instead of overflowing. Tested down to 375×667 (iPhone SE-class, the shortest common phone viewport) with room to spare; taller/wider viewports just get more breathing room via justify-content:center, not more content. If you add copy, keep the headline to one short line plus one accent word, and the dek to 1-2 short sentences — this layout has no scroll fallback, so it depends on staying terse.
